# decks — presentations

Pick the engine by what the owner needs at the end, not by what is easiest to generate.

| Part | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `parts/pptx/` | Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both |
| `parts/dashi-ppt/` | Build presentations from preset visual themes: offline HTML deck, editable in the browser, exportable to PPTX / PDF |
| `parts/lieflat-charts/` | Template-driven data visualization and report generation: HTML charts from the Lupi/Basics/Glance/Maps/Interactive galleries, plus 12 full-page report templates; Mono as the fallback, auto-selected by data semantics |
| `parts/slides/` | Create strategic HTML presentations with Chart.js, design tokens, responsive layouts, copywriting formulas, and contextual slide strategies |
| `parts/md-slides/` | Converts a markdown deck (slides separated by `---` HR boundaries or by `# ` H1 headings, with optional `<!-- notes:  |
| `parts/bento-slides/` | Create and edit Bento presentations — single-file .bento.html decks whose document is plain JSON in a "#bento-doc" script block |

## Choosing

- **A file someone opens in PowerPoint** -> `parts/pptx/` (reads and writes real
  `.pptx`; use it whenever a `.pptx` or `.potx` is involved at all).
- **An HTML deck that can be edited in the browser and exported** ->
  `parts/dashi-ppt/` (its generator runtime ships inside the part) or
  `parts/slides/` for Chart.js-driven decks.
- **Markdown already written, needs to become slides** -> `parts/md-slides/`.
- **A bento.page deck** -> `parts/bento-slides/`.
- **Charts and report pages with a fixed visual language** ->
  `parts/lieflat-charts/`.

`landing` (single-page landing sites) is in the `design` skill; diagrams belong
to `documents`.
